en: Steam from boiling water is hotter than the liquid itself and can cause severe skin burns.
Drinking saltwater dehydrates your body because your kidneys must use extra water to excrete the excess salt.
Mixing bleach with vinegar creates toxic chlorine gas, so you must never combine these two household cleaning liquids.
Storing chocolate in the refrigerator prevents melting because the cooler temperature removes the thermal energy needed to change its state.
Aerosol spray cans explode when heated because the gas inside expands and increases pressure beyond the metal container's limit.
You must shake liquid antibiotic suspensions before use to evenly distribute the solid medicine particles settled at the bottom.
Sweating cools your body because the liquid water absorbs heat from your skin to change into a gas.
Eating moldy bread is unsafe because the mold produces invisible chemical toxins that can make you very sick.
Wooden spoons are safer for stirring hot soup than metal spoons because wood is a poor heat conductor.
Washing greasy hands with just water fails because oil and water do not mix, so you must use soap.
Never touch dry ice with bare hands because its extreme cold temperature of minus seventy-nine degrees Celsius causes frostbite.
Swallowing button batteries is extremely dangerous because stomach acids trigger a chemical reaction that burns a hole in the esophagus.
